Summary of work: I was asked to validate a French grammar multiple-choice question about reported speech (discours indirect) and verb tense agreement (concordance des temps).

The question asks to complete: "Il a dit qu'il ___ à la réunion le lendemain."

The marked correct answer "viendrait" (conditionnel présent) is indeed correct. In French reported speech, when the main clause is in the past ("a dit" - passé composé), the future tense in the original direct speech shifts to the conditional. The original direct speech would have been "Il viendra à la réunion demain" (future), which becomes "Il viendrait à la réunion le lendemain" (conditional) in indirect speech.
